partners.diseaseBName: syndromic multisystem autoimmune disease due to ITCH deficiency
partners.mechanism_chain: FADD (HGNC:3794) —DISRUPTS→ Caspase activation and inflammatory signaling (REACT:R-HSA-300103); Caspase activation and inflammatory signaling (REACT:R-HSA-300103) —LEADS_TO→ Autoimmune disease (HP:0000708); ITCH (HGNC:18196) —DISRUPTS→ NF-kappaB signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-5691612); ITCH (HGNC:18196) —DISRUPTS→ Ubiquitin-mediated protein degradation (GO:0006511); Ubiquitin-mediated protein degradation (GO:0006511) —LEADS_TO→ NF-kappaB signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-5691612); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-5691612) —LEADS_TO→ Multisystem autoimmune disease (HP:0033742). FADD (involved in Disease A) is a key adaptor protein in death receptor signaling and can influence inflammatory pathways. Haploinsufficiency of FADD may lead to dysregulation of apoptotic and inflammatory cascades, contributing to autoimmune phenotypes. ITCH (causal in Disease B) is an E3 ubiquitin ligase that negatively regulates the NF-kappaB pathway by targeting key signaling proteins for degradation. Loss-of-function mutations in ITCH lead to accumulation of these targets, resulting in hyperactivation of NF-kappaB and promoting multisystem autoimmune disease. Both FADD and ITCH, through distinct mechanisms affecting the processing and signaling of inflammatory mediators, converge on the dysregulation of NF-kappaB signaling and related inflammatory pathways, ultimately leading to autoimmune manifestations.
